assets.statement: refuted at smallest parameters: r=2, k=2 family I₁={2,3}, I₂={24,25} gives total product 3600=60², exactly verified; Pell a(a+1)=6t² yields infinitely many length-2 square-product blocks, so k=2 imposes no obstruction and any close must use a fixed r across all k≥2 with explicit integrality.

L1 ("all positive integers are sums of ≤3 2-full numbers") refuted by n=7: powerful ≤7 are {1,4}, 3-term sums miss 7 (also n=15); canonical "large" hedge is load-bearing, so any close needs an explicit threshold/exception set.
positive upper density does not imply positive natural density (explicit block-set counterexample); repair: prove a uniform lower bound |S_C∩[1,N]| ≥ δN for all large N, never a limsup.

Finite-A periodic proof is domain drift: canonical ∀A⊆ℕ includes infinite A where periodicity/tail control vanishes; repair requires an analytic reduction (e.g. tail bounds uniform over all n∈A, m>x) or an explicit infinite-A counterexample with literal negation of the limit — neither exists on reco

Witness A={2^k} has a zero subsequence of (1_A*1_A)(n)/log n, so the nonzero-limit quantifier fails; any repair must prove a two-sided Θ(log n) bound for all sufficiently large n, not merely boundedness or a subsequence estimate.

Parity lemma refuted by Kummer: k&(n−k)=0 gives odd C(n,k); (7,3)=35 with lpf 5>7/2, and infinitely many (2^m−1,k) instances; branch-A close must instead bound small prime factors of odd coefficients directly.
